verdict_key.universal: Condemned by Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, and Protestant traditions
verdict_key.disputed: Condemned by some traditions, considered orthodox by others
verdict_key.tradition_specific: Condemned within one or two traditions only

heresies.name: Ebionitism
heresies.council_condemnation: Implicitly condemned at the Council of Nicaea (325); addressed by Irenaeus (c. 180) and Epiphanius in Panarion (c. 375)
fingerprints: Jesus was a natural-born human, the biological son of Joseph and Mary
Jesus was not divine by nature but was chosen or adopted by God at his baptism
Christ had no pre-existence before his earthly birth
The virgin birth is denied
Salvation requires full observance of the Mosaic Law
Paul was a false apostle and apostate from the Law
Jesus became the Son of God by merit or appointment, not by nature
The Old Testament Law is binding on all Christians
heresies.summary: Ebionitism denied the divinity and virgin birth of Christ, teaching he was a righteous man adopted by God at his baptism. It insisted on full Torah observance for salvation and rejected Paul entirely.

heresies.name: Docetism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Nicaea (325) and Council of Chalcedon (451); addressed by Ignatius of Antioch (c. 107) and Irenaeus (c. 180)
fingerprints: Christ only appeared to have a physical body
Christ only seemed to suffer and die
The divine cannot truly become material or flesh
Matter is inherently evil or inferior to spirit
Jesus was a purely spiritual being with a phantom or illusory body
The crucifixion was not a real physical event
The divine Christ departed from the human Jesus before the crucifixion
Christ did not truly experience human suffering
The resurrection was not a bodily resurrection
heresies.summary: Docetism taught that Christ only appeared to be human and only seemed to suffer and die. Rooted in the belief that matter is evil, it denied the true Incarnation and therefore undermined the reality of the atonement.

heresies.name: Gnosticism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned implicitly at Nicaea (325); refuted comprehensively by Irenaeus in Adversus Haereses (c. 180), Tertullian, Hippolytus, and Origen
fingerprints: The material world is evil or inferior and was created by a lesser or evil deity
The God of the Old Testament is an inferior, ignorant, or malevolent creator deity
The highest true God is entirely spiritual and remote from the material world
Salvation comes through secret knowledge (gnosis) rather than faith or grace
Certain humans contain a divine spark of light trapped in evil matter
Christ was a spiritual revealer of knowledge, not a true incarnate savior
The death of Christ has no atoning significance
The physical resurrection is denied or spiritualized
Scripture must be decoded through secret Gnostic interpretation
There are multiple levels of divine beings (aeons) between the highest God and the material world
The body and material existence are prisons to be escaped, not redeemed
heresies.summary: Gnosticism was a broad movement teaching radical dualism between spirit and matter, that the material world was created by an evil lesser god, and that salvation comes through secret spiritual knowledge rather than faith. It reinterpreted Christ as a spiritual revealer and denied the true Incarnation and atonement.

heresies.name: Marcionism
heresies.council_condemnation: Excommunicated by the Roman church (c. 144); refuted by Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, and Tertullian in Adversus Marcionem (5 books)
fingerprints: The God of the Old Testament and the God of the New Testament are two different Gods
The Old Testament God is inferior, wrathful, or evil
The Old Testament should be entirely rejected as Christian Scripture
Jesus revealed a previously unknown higher God of love
Christ had no real physical body and only appeared to be human
Paul is the only true apostle
The Christian canon should exclude the Old Testament entirely
The God of Israel is the source of evil or injustice in the world
The New Testament must be purged of Jewish or Old Testament influences
heresies.summary: Marcionism taught that the wrathful God of the Old Testament and the loving God revealed by Jesus were two entirely different deities. Marcion rejected the entire Old Testament, produced a truncated canon, and held a docetic view of Christ's body.

heresies.name: Montanism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by a series of Asian synods (late 2nd century); Apollinaris of Hierapolis and others wrote refutations; later condemned by Justinian's legislation (6th century)
fingerprints: New divine revelation continues after the apostolic age
The Holy Spirit speaks new binding truth through living prophets
New prophecy can supersede or add to Scripture
The apostolic deposit of faith is not the final or complete revelation
Specific living individuals are the direct mouthpiece of the Holy Spirit
The institutional church has no authority to test or reject prophetic claims
Moral requirements beyond Scripture are binding on all Christians
Martyrdom should be actively sought rather than avoided
Post-baptismal serious sins are unforgivable
heresies.summary: Montanism claimed that ongoing direct prophecy through Montanus and his associates superseded the apostolic tradition. Its core error was undermining the sufficiency and closure of Scripture by adding new binding divine revelation.

heresies.name: Modalism
heresies.council_condemnation: Sabellius excommunicated by Pope Callixtus I (c. 220); condemned at the First Council of Constantinople (381); refuted by Tertullian in Adversus Praxean (c. 213)
fingerprints: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not three distinct persons but three modes or masks of one person
God reveals himself successively as Father, then Son, then Spirit
The Father and the Son are the same person
The Father suffered and died on the cross
There is no real distinction between the persons of the Trinity
Jesus is the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit simultaneously
The Trinity is three names or titles for one divine person, not three persons
The Son has no distinct personal existence apart from the Father
Trinitarian distinctions in Scripture are merely different roles of the same person
heresies.summary: Modalism taught that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not three distinct persons but three successive modes or manifestations of one single divine person. It preserved divine unity but destroyed real Trinitarian distinction, and implied that the Father himself suffered on the cross.

heresies.name: Arianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Nicaea (325); reaffirmed and expanded at the First Council of Constantinople (381); the Nicene Creed is the primary anti-Arian document
fingerprints: Christ is a created being, not eternal God
There was a time when the Son did not exist
The Son was brought into existence by the Father before all ages
The Son is subordinate to the Father in nature and essence, not just in role
Christ is the greatest and first of all creatures but is still a creature
The Son is not of the same substance as the Father
The Son is similar to the Father but not equal in divine nature
Because the Son is a creature he is capable of change or moral failure
The Son did not exist before he was begotten or created by the Father
Calling Christ God is honorific, not a statement of his true nature
The Father alone is truly and fully God
heresies.summary: Arianism taught that the Son of God was the first and greatest of God's creatures, brought into being by the Father before all ages, but not co-eternal or co-equal with him. Its famous slogan was 'there was a time when he was not.' Because a created Christ cannot truly save, Arianism undermines the entire doctrine of salvation.

heresies.name: Donatism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Arles (314) and the Council of Milan (316); definitively ruled against at the Conference of Carthage (411); refuted extensively by Augustine of Hippo
fingerprints: The validity of a sacrament depends on the moral worthiness of the minister
A sinful or lapsed priest cannot administer valid sacraments
The church must be composed only of the morally pure
Baptism performed by an unworthy minister must be repeated
The holiness of the church depends on the holiness of its clergy
Those who compromised under persecution permanently forfeit their priestly authority
A pure remnant church is the only true church
Sacraments administered by traditors (those who handed over scriptures) are invalid
heresies.summary: Donatism taught that the validity of sacraments depended on the moral purity of the minister. Arising from the Diocletianic persecution, it formed a rigorist schismatic church claiming to be the only true church. Augustine's response established that sacraments are valid by Christ's action, not the minister's holiness.

heresies.name: Pelagianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Carthage (411 and 418) and Council of Ephesus (431); refuted extensively by Augustine of Hippo
fingerprints: Human beings are born morally neutral, not corrupted by original sin
The human will has full capacity to choose good without any divine grace
Adam's sin affected only Adam, not all of humanity
Original sin is merely a bad example set by Adam, not an inherited corruption or guilt
Grace is only external assistance such as the law, Scripture, or Christ's example
Salvation can be achieved by human moral effort and free will alone
People can choose God and initiate salvation entirely without divine assistance
Baptism does not remove an inherited sinful nature because none exists
Christ's work is primarily educational and exemplary, not substitutionary or atoning
Human nature after the Fall retains full and unimpaired capacity for righteousness
heresies.summary: Pelagianism held that humans are born with the same moral freedom as Adam before the Fall and can achieve righteousness without supernatural grace. It redefined grace as merely external aids like the law and Christ's example, effectively making salvation a human achievement and stripping Christ's death of redemptive necessity.

heresies.name: Semi-Pelagianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Second Council of Orange (529), which affirmed Augustinian grace against it
fingerprints: The first movement toward God — the initial desire for salvation — comes from human will unaided by grace
Grace is necessary for perseverance and completion of salvation but not for its initiation
God gives grace in response to the human will's initial unaided movement toward him
Human beings retain enough goodness after the Fall to begin seeking God without assistance
Faith begins as a human act before grace responds and cooperates with it
God's election is based on his foreknowledge of who will freely choose him first
The will and grace cooperate as equal partners in initiating salvation
heresies.summary: Semi-Pelagianism moderated full Pelagianism by acknowledging that grace is necessary for completing salvation, but taught that the initial movement toward God — the first step of faith — comes from the human will unaided by divine grace. Condemned at Orange (529), which affirmed that even the beginning of faith is a gift of grace.

heresies.name: Nestorianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Ephesus (431); refined at the Council of Chalcedon (451); Nestorius was deposed and exiled
fingerprints: Christ is two persons loosely joined rather than one person
The divine Son and the human Jesus are distinct persons united by moral or relational union
Mary gave birth to the human person Jesus only, not to God incarnate
Mary should not be called Theotokos (God-bearer or Mother of God)
The divine nature and human nature in Christ are so distinct they constitute separate subjects
The union of divine and human in Christ is one of will or relationship, not of person
God the Son did not truly suffer and die because the suffering belonged to the human person only
The Incarnation is a close cooperation between a divine person and a human person
heresies.summary: Nestorianism so strongly divided Christ's two natures that it was charged with teaching two persons — a divine Son and a human Jesus — joined by a moral rather than a true personal union. This fractured the Incarnation and undermined the atonement, since the divine Son would not have truly suffered and died.

heresies.name: Eutychianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Chalcedon (451), which defined Christ as one person in two natures without confusion, change, division, or separation; Eutyches was deposed
fingerprints: Christ's human nature was absorbed into or overwhelmed by his divine nature
After the Incarnation Christ has only one nature, not two
The human nature of Christ was dissolved into the divine like a drop in the ocean
Christ did not retain a full and complete human nature after the Incarnation
The divine nature consumed or replaced the human nature in Christ
Christ is not truly consubstantial with humanity after the union of natures
The two natures of Christ were mixed or blended into a single new nature
Christ's humanity was not the same kind of humanity as ours
heresies.summary: Eutychianism taught that Christ's human nature was absorbed into his divine nature at the Incarnation, leaving only one nature. A reaction against Nestorianism, it went too far in the opposite direction and effectively denied the full humanity of Christ, undermining the atonement just as Docetism does.

heresies.name: Apollinarianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the First Council of Constantinople (381); refuted by Gregory of Nazianzus in Epistles 101 and 102
fingerprints: The divine Logos replaced the human rational soul or mind of Christ
Christ did not have a complete human nature because his rational soul was divine
Christ had a human body but not a full human rational or spiritual nature
The divine nature of Christ substituted for the highest part of his humanity
Christ's person was composed of a human body and the divine Logos, with no human mind
A complete human rational soul in Christ would threaten the unity of his person
What is not assumed by Christ is not redeemed
heresies.summary: Apollinarianism taught that in the Incarnation the divine Logos replaced Christ's human rational soul, leaving him with a human body but no complete human mind or spirit. Gregory of Nazianzus delivered the decisive refutation: what Christ did not assume, he did not redeem — meaning an incomplete humanity leaves humanity incompletely saved.

heresies.name: Manichaeism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by Roman imperial edict under Diocletian (297); refuted extensively by Augustine of Hippo in Contra Faustum, De Moribus Manichaeorum, and De Natura Boni
fingerprints: Good and evil are two co-eternal and equal cosmic principles
The material world is inherently evil and was created by a dark or evil force
The human body is a prison of evil matter trapping a divine spark of light
Salvation means escaping from matter and returning the soul to the realm of light
The God of light did not create the physical world
Christ, Buddha, and other figures were spiritual enlighteners, not unique saviors
The physical body of Christ was not real — he was a purely spiritual being
The Old Testament God is an evil or lesser deity associated with darkness
There are two tiers of the saved — the fully enlightened and their supporters
Marriage and procreation are evil because they trap more light particles in matter
heresies.summary: Manichaeism was a syncretic dualist religion blending Zoroastrian, Buddhist, Gnostic, and Christian elements. It taught that good and evil are co-eternal cosmic forces, that matter is evil, and that salvation means liberating divine light-sparks from material imprisonment. Its Christ was purely spiritual with no real body or atoning death.

heresies.name: Iconoclasm
heresies.tradition_notes: Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions condemn Iconoclasm as heresy, settled definitively at the Second Council of Nicaea (787). Many Protestant traditions, however, share some iconoclast concerns about religious images, particularly in the Reformed tradition, and do not consider the veneration of icons to be required or the rejection of them to be heretical. The Protestant verdict here is therefore disputed rather than a clear condemnation of Iconoclasm as heresy.
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Second Council of Nicaea (787), the seventh ecumenical council; icon veneration definitively restored at the Triumph of Orthodoxy (843)
fingerprints: Depicting Christ or the saints in images is forbidden by God
Venerating religious images is always equivalent to idolatry
The divine nature of Christ cannot and should not be depicted in art
All physical representations of Christ or holy persons must be destroyed
The Incarnation does not change the prohibition on depicting God
Any honor given to a religious image is worship given to a material object
The use of icons in worship is a corruption imported from paganism
heresies.summary: Byzantine Iconoclasm was the movement, largely driven by imperial power, to destroy religious images and prohibit their veneration. Orthodox and Catholic traditions condemn it as heresy, settled at Nicaea II (787). Many Protestant traditions share concerns about image veneration and do not consider rejection of icons to be heretical, making this a disputed verdict.

heresies.name: Paulicianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by Byzantine imperial edicts; violently persecuted under Empress Theodora (c. 843); refuted in Byzantine theological literature
fingerprints: The material world was created by an evil principle or being
The God of the Old Testament is an evil or lesser deity
The Old Testament should be entirely rejected
Christ did not have a real physical body
The crucifixion and resurrection were not physical events
All sacraments are invalid or unnecessary
The cross as a symbol should be rejected
The church hierarchy and institutional church are corrupt or illegitimate
Mary should not be venerated as the Mother of God
heresies.summary: Paulicianism was a dualist movement originating in Armenia that rejected the material world as the creation of an evil principle, held a docetic Christology, and rejected the Old Testament, sacraments, church hierarchy, and veneration of Mary. It was a significant predecessor to later medieval dualist movements like Bogomilism and Catharism.

heresies.name: Bogomilism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by local Bulgarian church councils and Byzantine synods; refuted by Euthymius Zigabenus in the Dogmatic Panoply (c. 1100) commissioned by Emperor Alexios I
fingerprints: The material world was created by Satan or a fallen divine being, not the true God
Satan is identified with the God of the Old Testament or as a fallen son of God
The true God is entirely spiritual and had no role in creating the physical world
Christ was a purely spiritual being who did not truly become flesh
The cross is a symbol of evil and should be rejected
All material sacraments are invalid and should be rejected
The institutional church is a Satanic institution
The Old Testament should be entirely rejected
Marriage and reproduction are evil because they perpetuate material existence
There are two tiers of believers — the perfect inner circle and ordinary followers
The resurrection of the body is denied
heresies.summary: Bogomilism was a dualist gnostic movement from 10th-century Bulgaria teaching that Satan created the material world and that Christ was a purely spiritual being. It rejected sacraments, the cross, church hierarchy, and the Old Testament. It was a direct predecessor to Catharism in Western Europe.

heresies.name: Catharism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at Lateran III (1179) and Lateran IV (1215); the Albigensian Crusade launched by Pope Innocent III (1209–1229); the fall of Montségur (1244) effectively ended organized Catharism
fingerprints: The material world is the creation of an evil god or principle
The true God of love is entirely spiritual and did not create physical matter
The God of the Old Testament is evil or a lesser deity
Christ was a divine spiritual being who only appeared to have a physical body
The crucifixion and resurrection were not real physical events
The Catholic Church and its sacraments are institutions of the evil creator
The consolamentum — a spiritual baptism — is the only valid sacrament
Procreation is evil because it traps divine sparks in evil matter
There are two classes of believers — the perfecti and the credentes
The resurrection of the body is denied — only spiritual liberation matters
Eating meat and other products of reproduction is forbidden for the perfect
The cross should be rejected as a symbol of evil, not venerated
heresies.summary: Catharism was the most widespread medieval dualist heresy, flourishing in southern France and northern Italy. It taught that the material world was created by an evil god, that Christ was a purely spiritual being, and that the Catholic Church was satanic. It was suppressed by crusade and inquisition over the 13th and 14th centuries.

heresies.name: Waldensians
heresies.tradition_notes: The Waldensians were condemned as heretics by the medieval Catholic Church primarily for unauthorized preaching and later for positions anticipating the Reformation — rejection of purgatory, critique of unworthy clergy, and emphasis on Scripture. Protestant traditions largely regard the Waldensians as proto-Reformers rather than heretics. The Waldensian church itself aligned with Reformed Protestantism in 1532 and exists today. This entry reflects their condemned medieval positions, not their later Reformed theology.
heresies.council_condemnation: Excommunicated by Pope Lucius III at the Synod of Verona (1184); condemned at Lateran III and IV; subject to Inquisition proceedings
fingerprints: Lay people have the right and duty to preach Scripture without ecclesiastical authorization
The validity of sacraments depends on the moral worthiness of the priest
Purgatory does not exist
Prayers and masses for the dead are without value
The institutional church has forfeited its authority through moral corruption
Scripture alone is the sufficient rule of faith and practice
Oaths are forbidden by Christ's teaching
Capital punishment is always wrong
heresies.summary: The Waldensians began as a lay poverty and preaching movement condemned by Rome for unauthorized preaching. Over time they developed positions anticipating the Reformation — rejecting purgatory, critiquing clerical authority, and elevating Scripture. Protestant traditions generally regard them as proto-Reformers rather than heretics. Their entry here reflects the positions for which they were condemned.

heresies.name: Joachimism
heresies.council_condemnation: Joachim's specific trinitarian views condemned at Lateran IV (1215); Gerard of Borgo San Donnino's Introductorius condemned (1255); Fra Dolcino executed (1307); Spiritual Franciscans condemned by Pope John XXII (1317–1324)
fingerprints: History is divided into three ages corresponding to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
A coming Age of the Spirit will supersede the current Age of the Son
The institutional church and papacy will become obsolete in the coming spiritual age
A new Eternal Gospel will supersede the New Testament
Specific historical figures are identifiable as the Antichrist
A new order of spiritual monks will replace the current church hierarchy
New divine revelation has been given about the imminent end of the current age
The Pope or institutional church is the Whore of Babylon
The current age of Scripture and sacrament will be replaced by direct spiritual illumination
heresies.summary: Joachimism drew on the visions of Joachim of Fiore to teach that history moves through three ages — Father, Son, and Spirit — and that the institutional church would soon be superseded by a new age of direct spiritual illumination. Radical followers identified the Pope as Antichrist and claimed a new Eternal Gospel would replace the New Testament.

heresies.name: Flagellantism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by Pope Clement VI in the bull Inter Sollicitudines (1349); condemned at the Council of Constance (1415); pursued by local inquisitions through the 15th century
fingerprints: Self-inflicted physical suffering can atone for sin
Human suffering is redemptively equivalent to or a supplement of Christ's atoning work
Christ's atonement is insufficient and requires human suffering to complete it
Performing acts of bodily penance removes the guilt of sin directly
The church and its sacraments are unnecessary for those who perform sufficient self-punishment
Direct divine revelation authorizes and commands acts of severe self-mortification
Physical suffering earns merit before God that offsets the penalty of sin
heresies.summary: Flagellantism arose especially during the Black Death (1347–1351), when groups publicly whipped themselves as corporate penance. The heretical extreme taught that self-inflicted suffering was itself redemptively sufficient — effectively claiming that human pain could complete or replace what Christ's death accomplished, undermining the sufficiency of the atonement.

heresies.name: Hussitism (Radical Wing)
heresies.tradition_notes: The mainstream Hussite position — Utraquism, receiving communion in both bread and wine — is considered by many Protestant traditions to be a legitimate reform rather than a heresy, and Jan Hus himself is regarded as a proto-Reformer by Luther and others. This entry covers the radical Taborite and Pikart wing specifically, whose rejection of the Real Presence, sacraments, and church hierarchy goes beyond what most Protestant traditions would endorse. Catholic and Orthodox traditions condemn the movement broadly; Protestant traditions distinguish between Hus and the radical wing.
heresies.council_condemnation: Jan Hus condemned and burned at the Council of Constance (1415); John Wycliffe condemned posthumously at the same council; crusade bulls issued against the Hussites; Taborite positions condemned at Constance
fingerprints: The Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist is denied entirely
The institutional church and its sacraments have no valid authority
Purgatory does not exist
Veneration of saints and relics is forbidden idolatry
The Pope is the Antichrist
Direct divine illumination supersedes the authority of Scripture and tradition
All external religious observance is unnecessary for the truly spiritual
The truly enlightened are beyond ordinary moral constraints
Private ownership of property is sinful and should be abolished on Christian grounds
heresies.summary: The radical wing of the Hussite movement went far beyond Jan Hus's own positions, denying the Real Presence, rejecting all sacraments and church authority, and in the most extreme Pikart strand claiming that the truly spiritual are beyond external moral law. Protestant traditions distinguish sharply between Hus as proto-Reformer and the radical Taborite positions condemned here.

heresies.name: Antinomianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned in the Lutheran tradition by the Formula of Concord (1577), Articles V and VI; addressed by Calvin in the Institutes; condemned by the Westminster Confession (1646)
fingerprints: Christians are entirely free from any obligation to the moral law
The law has no role whatsoever in the Christian life — not for conviction, guidance, or sanctification
Because salvation is by grace alone, moral conduct is irrelevant to the Christian
The truly spiritual person is incapable of sin or is beyond moral categories
Sins committed by believers have no moral significance because they are already forgiven
The Holy Spirit leads Christians in ways that may contradict the moral law of Scripture
Preaching the law to Christians is a denial of grace
Obedience to moral commands is a form of works-righteousness to be rejected
The inner spiritual life overrides all external moral standards
heresies.summary: Antinomianism taught that because Christians are saved by grace through faith alone, the moral law has no binding role in the Christian life. Extreme forms concluded that the truly spiritual person cannot sin or is beyond moral categories entirely. All major Protestant confessions, alongside Catholic and Orthodox teaching, condemned this as a distortion of grace.

heresies.name: Socinianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Polish Brethren expelled from Poland by the Sejm (1658); condemned in Reformed confessions and by Lutheran orthodoxy; the Racovian Catechism (1605) was the primary document condemned
fingerprints: The Trinity is a false doctrine — God is strictly one person, the Father
Christ is not co-eternal God but a created and exalted human being
Christ preexisted only in God's foreknowledge, not ontologically
Christ's death was not a satisfaction for sin or a penal substitution
The atonement is a moral example and demonstration of forgiveness, not a legal transaction
Hell as eternal conscious punishment does not exist
Original sin in its traditional sense is denied
Human reason is the final arbiter of all theological claims including Scripture
Salvation is achieved through moral improvement and obedience aided by Christ's example
The Holy Spirit is not a distinct divine person
Miracles and supernatural elements of Scripture should be interpreted rationally
heresies.summary: Socinianism was the most thoroughgoing rationalist critique of orthodox Christianity in the Reformation era. It denied the Trinity, the pre-existence of Christ, penal substitutionary atonement, original sin, and eternal punishment. It treated human reason as the supreme theological authority and anticipated Enlightenment Unitarianism directly.

heresies.name: Anabaptist Radicalism
heresies.tradition_notes: This entry covers the radical wing of Anabaptism specifically — the Münsterites, Thomas Müntzer, and Melchiorite Christology — not mainstream Anabaptism. Mainstream Anabaptist groups such as the Swiss Brethren, Mennonites, and Hutterites held largely orthodox Trinitarian and Christological positions and are considered by many Protestant traditions to be legitimate if non-conformist expressions of Christian faith. The radical positions covered here — violent theocracy, ongoing revelation superseding Scripture, and docetic Christology — are condemned across traditions.
heresies.council_condemnation: Münster commune crushed by military force (1535); Jan of Leiden executed; condemned by the Second Diet of Speyer (1529) and various imperial edicts; refuted by Luther, Zwingli, and Calvin
fingerprints: Direct ongoing divine revelation supersedes and corrects Scripture
God calls his people to violent revolutionary action to establish his kingdom now
A theocratic political kingdom should be established by force before Christ's return
The truly Spirit-filled leader is above ordinary moral and scriptural constraints
Polygamy is permitted or commanded for leaders of the renewed community
Christ did not take on flesh from Mary — he passed through her like water through a pipe
The inner voice of the Spirit carries more authority than the written Word
The institutional church must be violently overthrown to prepare for the kingdom
Baptism and other sacraments are obstacles to pure Spirit-led religion
heresies.summary: The radical wing of Anabaptism — the Münsterites, Müntzer, and Melchiorite groups — combined apocalyptic violence, claims of direct revelation superseding Scripture, and in some cases a docetic Christology denying Christ took flesh from Mary. This entry does not represent mainstream Anabaptism, which is broadly considered orthodox in its Christology.

heresies.name: Familism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned by edicts in the Netherlands and England; Queen Elizabeth I issued proclamations against Familism (1580); refuted by various Reformed and Anglican writers
fingerprints: The writings of a living spiritual leader are equal to or surpass Scripture in authority
True religion consists in being deified or merged into God through love
Heaven and hell are purely internal spiritual states, not future realities
The resurrection and final judgment are entirely spiritual or allegorical events
The truly enlightened are above all external religious observance
Attending any church while holding private esoteric beliefs is acceptable
Inner spiritual experience is the only true measure of salvation
Outward conformity to any religion is permissible because external forms are irrelevant
A living prophet has received divine inspiration equivalent to Scripture
heresies.summary: Familism was a mystical sect teaching that true religion meant being deified through love, that heaven and hell were inner spiritual states, and that the enlightened were above external religious forms. Its founder Hendrik Niclaes claimed his writings were divinely inspired. Members practiced deliberate dissimulation — attending any church while privately holding Familist beliefs.

heresies.name: Arminianism
heresies.tradition_notes: Arminianism is condemned as heresy within the Reformed and Calvinist tradition, which regards it as a form of semi-Pelagianism that undermines divine sovereignty in salvation. However it is considered fully orthodox within Methodist, Wesleyan, General Baptist, Pentecostal, and many other Protestant traditions. Catholic and Eastern Orthodox theology is broadly compatible with Arminian positions on grace and free will — both traditions affirm resistible grace and conditional election in ways similar to Arminius. The app should never return a flat heresy verdict for Arminianism without prominently noting this disagreement.
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned within the Reformed tradition at the Synod of Dort (1618–1619), which produced the Canons of Dort; Remonstrant ministers were expelled from the Dutch Reformed Church
fingerprints: God's election of individuals to salvation is conditional on his foreknowledge of their faith
Christ died for all people without exception, not only for the elect
Saving grace can be resisted and rejected by the human will
A genuinely saved person can fall away from grace and lose their salvation
Prevenient grace restores free will so humans can accept or reject the gospel
God's predestination is based on his foreknowledge of human choices rather than his sovereign decree
The atonement is unlimited in its scope and intended for every person
heresies.summary: Arminianism holds that election is conditional on foreknown faith, that Christ died for all, that grace is resistible, and that salvation can be lost. Condemned at the Synod of Dort (1619) within the Reformed tradition as undermining divine sovereignty, it is considered fully orthodox by Methodist, Wesleyan, Catholic, and Eastern Orthodox traditions. This is one of the most significant intra-Protestant theological disputes.

heresies.name: Jansenism
heresies.tradition_notes: Jansenism is condemned as heresy by the Catholic Church through multiple papal bulls, primarily for its specific propositions about irresistible grace, the impossibility of keeping some commandments, and its rigorist sacramental practice. Eastern Orthodox theology has no formal verdict on Jansenism as it was an internal Catholic controversy. Many Protestant and Reformed theologians find Jansenist positions on grace largely compatible with Augustinian and Calvinist theology — the five condemned propositions resemble Reformed positions closely. The condemnation is therefore specifically Catholic in its force.
heresies.council_condemnation: Five propositions condemned by Pope Innocent X in Cum Occasione (1653); 101 Jansenist propositions condemned by Pope Clement XI in Unigenitus (1713)
fingerprints: Some of God's commandments are impossible for the justified to keep even with available grace
Interior grace is irresistible and cannot be refused by the human will
For an act to be meritorious or sinful it must be free from all external necessity but not from internal necessity
Semi-Pelagians were wrong to teach that the human will can resist or assent to grace
It is Semi-Pelagian to say Christ died for all people without exception
Frequent communion should be restricted to those who have achieved a high degree of moral purity
Absolution should be withheld until the penitent has demonstrated sustained moral reform
The institutional church has compromised the rigor of authentic Augustinian Christianity
heresies.summary: Jansenism was a Catholic theological movement claiming to recover Augustinian teaching on grace against Jesuit semi-Pelagianism. Condemned by Rome through multiple bulls, its five core propositions were judged to make grace irresistible and some commandments impossible. Many Protestant and Reformed theologians find the condemned positions compatible with their own theology, making this primarily a Catholic condemnation.

heresies.name: Deism
heresies.council_condemnation: Not formally condemned by a single council; addressed by Anglican, Reformed, Lutheran, and Catholic theologians including William Paley in Natural Theology and Joseph Butler in The Analogy of Religion; condemned implicitly by all confessional standards
fingerprints: God created the universe but does not intervene in it or human history
Miracles are impossible or have never occurred
God does not answer prayer or act providentially in the world
Divine revelation through Scripture or prophets is impossible or unnecessary
Jesus was a great moral teacher but not God incarnate
The resurrection did not occur as a supernatural event
Religion should be reduced to universal rational morality
The supernatural elements of Christianity are myth or priestly invention
Human reason alone is sufficient to know God and moral duty
God is an absentee creator with no ongoing relationship with creation
The particular historical claims of Christianity are irrelevant to true religion
heresies.summary: Deism held that God created the universe and its rational laws but does not intervene in history — no miracles, revelation, incarnation, resurrection, or providence. Religion was reduced to universal rational morality. It stripped Christianity of every particular historical and theological claim, effectively dismantling it while retaining the word God.

heresies.name: Unitarianism
heresies.council_condemnation: Trinitarian orthodoxy defined at Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381) stands as the primary condemnation; Michael Servetus condemned and executed in Geneva (1553); condemned by all major Protestant confessions
fingerprints: God is strictly one person — the Father — not a Trinity of three persons
Jesus was a preeminent human teacher and moral example but not divine
The doctrine of the Trinity is a later corruption of original Christianity
The Holy Spirit is not a distinct divine person
Original sin and the Fall are myths or metaphors with no doctrinal weight
Penal substitutionary atonement is a morally repugnant doctrine to be rejected
Hell as eternal conscious punishment does not exist
All religious traditions are equally valid paths to the divine
Scripture is a human document to be read through rational and moral criticism
Creeds and confessions have no binding authority on Christian belief
Jesus's significance lies in his moral teaching and example, not his person or atoning work
heresies.summary: Unitarianism denied the Trinity, holding God to be strictly one person and Jesus to be a supreme moral teacher but not divine. Drawing on Socinian and Enlightenment rationalist roots it also rejected original sin, substitutionary atonement, and eternal punishment. Modern Unitarian Universalism has largely moved beyond Christianity altogether.

heresies.name: Mormonism
alternate_names: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils as Mormonism postdates them; condemned as non-Christian by Catholic, Orthodox, and major Protestant bodies; addressed in Walter Martin's Kingdom of the Cults and numerous evangelical responses
fingerprints: God the Father was once a mortal man who progressed to divinity
There are multiple gods — the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are three entirely separate divine beings
Human beings are the literal spirit children of God and a Heavenly Mother
Faithful humans can progress to become gods themselves
The apostolic church was entirely lost and required restoration through Joseph Smith
The Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants, and Pearl of Great Price are Scripture equal to or surpassing the Bible
A living prophet receives new binding divine revelation that can supersede previous Scripture
Salvation in its fullest sense requires Mormon temple ordinances
Jesus and Lucifer are spirit brothers — both literal sons of the Heavenly Father
The God of Christianity prior to Joseph Smith was a false or incomplete understanding of God
Exaltation — becoming a god — is the ultimate goal of human existence
heresies.summary: Mormonism departs from orthodox Christianity on nearly every foundational doctrine — the nature of God, the Trinity, the uniqueness of Christ, the sufficiency of Scripture, and the nature of salvation. Its teaching that God was once a mortal man and that humans can become gods represents a fundamental break with the monotheism and Christology of historic Christianity across all three traditions.

heresies.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils; condemned as a modern form of Arianism by Catholic, Orthodox, and mainstream Protestant traditions; the New World Translation's rendering of John 1:1 as 'a god' is rejected by mainstream biblical scholarship
fingerprints: Christ is Michael the Archangel — the first and greatest of God's creations
Christ is not co-equal or co-eternal with God the Father
The Holy Spirit is not a divine person but an impersonal active force
The doctrine of the Trinity is a pagan corruption of original Christianity
Christ did not rise bodily — his physical body was dissolved and he rose as a spirit being
The human soul does not survive death — the dead are unconscious until resurrection
Hell as a place of conscious punishment does not exist — the wicked are annihilated
Only 144,000 people will reign with Christ in heaven
The majority of the faithful will live eternally on a restored earthly paradise
Blood transfusions are forbidden by Scripture
Celebrating birthdays, Christmas, and Easter is forbidden as pagan
heresies.summary: Jehovah's Witnesses revive an essentially Arian Christology, teaching that Christ is Michael the Archangel and the first of God's creations rather than co-eternal God. They deny the Trinity, the bodily resurrection, the conscious afterlife, and eternal punishment. Their New World Translation alters key Trinitarian texts to support these positions.

heresies.name: Christian Science
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils; rejected by mainstream Christian traditions as departing fundamentally from biblical theology; Mary Baker Eddy's Science and Health treated as co-equal with Scripture
fingerprints: Matter does not truly exist — only spirit and mind are real
Disease, sin, and death are illusions of mortal mind with no ultimate reality
God is the only reality — all else including the physical world is illusion or error
Christ's work was a demonstration of the unreality of sin and death, not an atoning sacrifice
Salvation is achieved by correcting false mental beliefs, not by faith in Christ's death
Medical treatment reinforces the illusion of material disease and should be avoided
The physical body and its suffering are not real
The resurrection demonstrated the illusion of death rather than a real bodily event
Sin is primarily ignorance or wrong thinking rather than moral rebellion against God
Mary Baker Eddy's writings provide the key to correctly interpreting Scripture
heresies.summary: Christian Science teaches a thoroughgoing idealist metaphysics in which matter, disease, and death are illusions of mortal mind. God alone is real. Christ demonstrated the unreality of sin and death rather than atoning for sin. Salvation comes through correcting false thinking. The denial of material reality makes the Incarnation, bodily resurrection, and substitutionary atonement all impossible.

heresies.name: Prosperity Gospel
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils; condemned by a broad coalition of evangelical scholars; addressed critically by the Evangelical Theological Society and numerous Reformed, Lutheran, Catholic, and Orthodox writers; D.R. McConnell's A Different Gospel provides a scholarly critique
fingerprints: Financial wealth and physical health are the guaranteed covenant rights of every Christian
Poverty and sickness are always the result of insufficient faith or unconfessed sin
Faith is a spiritual force or law that produces results when activated by correct speech
Positive verbal confession of desired outcomes causes them to materialize
Christ's atonement secured physical healing and financial prosperity in addition to forgiveness
Giving money to a ministry or pastor activates a divine law of financial return
Believers are divine beings or little gods with the same class of nature as God
Christ suffered spiritual death and torment in hell as part of the atonement
God is obligated to bless believers materially when they exercise sufficient faith
Suffering, poverty, or illness in a Christian's life indicates a faith failure
The primary purpose of salvation includes earthly comfort, success, and prosperity
heresies.summary: The Prosperity Gospel teaches that financial wealth and physical health are covenant rights secured by Christ's atonement and obtained through faith, positive confession, and giving. It reduces faith to a spiritual force, makes God obligated to material blessing, and implies that suffering reflects inadequate faith. It is condemned across Catholic, Orthodox, and mainstream Protestant traditions.

heresies.name: Oneness Pentecostalism
heresies.council_condemnation: The ancient form — Sabellianism — was condemned by Pope Callixtus I (c. 220) and at Constantinople (381); modern Oneness Pentecostalism was expelled from the Assemblies of God (1916) following their adoption of the Statement of Fundamental Truths affirming Trinitarian orthodoxy
fingerprints: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not three distinct persons but three titles for one person — Jesus
Jesus is the full name of God — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are all manifestations of Jesus alone
The Trinitarian baptismal formula of Matthew 28:19 should be replaced with baptism in Jesus name only
Baptism in Jesus name only is required for salvation
Speaking in tongues is the necessary initial evidence of the Holy Spirit and required for salvation
The doctrine of the Trinity is a pagan corruption introduced after the apostolic age
There is no personal distinction between the Father and the Son — they are the same person
The Father did not send the Son as a distinct person — Jesus is himself the Father incarnate
heresies.summary: Oneness Pentecostalism is a modern revival of ancient Modalism, teaching that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not three distinct persons but three titles or manifestations of the one God who is Jesus. It requires baptism in Jesus name only and tongues-speaking for salvation. Expelled from the Assemblies of God in 1916 and condemned by all Trinitarian traditions.

heresies.name: Open Theism
heresies.tradition_notes: Open Theism is condemned by Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions as incompatible with classical divine omniscience and the doctrine of God. Within Protestantism it is treated as outside orthodoxy by Reformed, Lutheran, and most evangelical bodies — the Evangelical Theological Society asked open theist members to resign in 2003. However a minority of evangelical theologians argue it represents a legitimate intra-evangelical position rather than a heresy proper. The verdict is disputed within Protestantism though rejected by Catholic and Orthodox traditions clearly.
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils directly; condemned by the Evangelical Theological Society (2003); rejected by Reformed, Lutheran, Catholic, and Orthodox traditions; addressed by the Southern Baptist Convention
fingerprints: God does not exhaustively foreknow future free human choices
The future is genuinely open and unknowable even to God because it does not yet exist
God takes risks in creation because he cannot know with certainty how free creatures will choose
God learns, adjusts, and responds to human decisions in real time
Biblical passages where God repents or changes his mind describe real changes in God's knowledge or intention
Exhaustive divine foreknowledge is incompatible with genuine human freedom
God's omniscience covers all past and present reality but not the undetermined future
The certainty of biblical prophecy is based on God's power to ensure outcomes not on foreknowledge
heresies.summary: Open Theism holds that God does not exhaustively foreknow future free human choices — the future is genuinely open even to God. Presented as the best way to preserve human freedom and explain biblical passages where God changes his mind, it is rejected by Catholic and Orthodox traditions and by most Protestant bodies as incompatible with classical divine omniscience and the certainty of redemptive promises.

heresies.name: Progressive Christianity
heresies.tradition_notes: Progressive Christianity is a broad and varied movement. At its moderate end it represents theological liberalism with which some Protestant denominations have significant sympathy. At its radical end — denying the bodily resurrection, the uniqueness of Christ, the authority of Scripture, and traditional sexual ethics — it departs from historic Christianity so thoroughly that Catholic, Orthodox, and most Protestant traditions regard it as outside orthodox Christianity. The disputed verdict reflects the spectrum: moderate progressive positions are debated within mainline Protestantism while the most radical positions are condemned across traditions. The fingerprints below reflect the more clearly heterodox positions within the movement.
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils; the Catholic Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith addressed related themes in Dominus Iesus (2000); the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy (1978) addresses the biblical authority questions involved
fingerprints: The bodily resurrection of Christ did not occur as a historical physical event
Jesus is one valid path to God among many — other religions are equally salvific
The Bible is a purely human document with no unique divine authority
The substitutionary atonement is a morally primitive or repugnant doctrine to be rejected
Traditional sexual ethics are cultural constructs with no binding biblical authority
Sin is primarily structural and social rather than personal moral rebellion against God
Hell as a place of conscious punishment does not exist
The creeds and confessions of historic Christianity are not binding on contemporary believers
Christian identity can be maintained while rejecting the supernatural claims of the faith
God is not a personal being who acts in history but a metaphor for human values or love
The virgin birth is a theological symbol rather than a historical event
heresies.summary: Progressive Christianity is a broad movement ranging from moderate theological liberalism to radical revisionism. At its furthest extent it denies the bodily resurrection, the uniqueness of Christ, the authority of Scripture, and substitutionary atonement while retaining Christian language. Catholic and Orthodox traditions condemn the radical positions clearly; the verdict within Protestantism depends heavily on which specific claims are in view.

heresies.name: Adoptionism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Antioch (268) in the case of Paul of Samosata; elements condemned at Nicaea (325); the Spanish form condemned at the Council of Frankfurt (794) and Council of Rome (799)
fingerprints: Jesus was born an ordinary human being with no divine pre-existence
God adopted Jesus as his Son at a specific moment — his baptism, resurrection, or birth
Jesus became the Son of God by divine appointment or reward for his righteousness
Christ had no existence as the eternal Son before his human birth
The divine sonship of Jesus is a status conferred upon him, not a nature he possesses eternally
Jesus was elevated to divine status because of his perfect obedience
God dwelt in Jesus as in a temple or vessel but Jesus was not himself God by nature
The title Son of God describes a role or relationship, not an eternal ontological reality
There was a moment in time when Jesus became or was declared the Son of God
heresies.summary: Adoptionism taught that Jesus was born a fully human being who was later adopted or appointed as the Son of God — typically at his baptism or resurrection — as a reward for his perfect righteousness. It denies the eternal pre-existence of the Son and reduces divine sonship to an honorary status rather than an eternal nature. It recurs across different periods and is the Christological error most closely associated with modern liberal theology's view of Jesus as an inspired human being.

heresies.name: Subordinationism
heresies.council_condemnation: Condemned at the Council of Nicaea (325) and First Council of Constantinople (381), which defined the Son as homoousios — of the same substance — with the Father and affirmed the full divinity of the Holy Spirit
fingerprints: The Son is lesser than the Father in divine nature or essence, not merely in role
The Holy Spirit is lesser in divine nature than the Father and Son
There is a hierarchy of being within the Trinity — the Father is more fully divine
The Son derives his divine nature from the Father making him secondary in essence
The persons of the Trinity are unequal in their divine attributes or perfections
The Father alone possesses the fullness of divinity — the Son and Spirit share it partially or derivatively
The Son is eternally begotten in a way that makes him ontologically inferior to the Father
Worship and prayer should be directed primarily or exclusively to the Father as the supreme deity
heresies.summary: Subordinationism teaches that the Son and Holy Spirit are lesser than the Father in their divine nature or essence — not merely in their eternal roles or missions. It is the broad category of which Arianism is the most extreme form. It must be carefully distinguished from the orthodox doctrine of eternal functional subordination, which holds that the Son submits to the Father in role and mission while remaining fully equal in divine nature and essence.

heresies.name: Kenosis (Heretical Form)
heresies.council_condemnation: Not addressed by ancient councils as the modern controversy postdates them; condemned by Catholic, Orthodox, and mainstream Protestant theologians as incompatible with the full divinity of Christ and Chalcedonian Christology
fingerprints: Christ permanently surrendered or gave up his divine attributes at the Incarnation
The incarnate Christ was not omniscient — he genuinely did not know things as a result of emptying himself of divine knowledge
The incarnate Christ was not omnipotent — he genuinely lacked divine power as a result of the kenosis
The incarnate Christ was not omnipresent — he was spatially limited not merely by choice but by nature during the Incarnation
Christ ceased to be fully God during his earthly life because he emptied himself of divine attributes
The kenosis involved an actual ontological diminishment of Christ's divine nature
Christ had to reacquire or have restored his divine attributes after the resurrection
The self-emptying of Philippians 2:7 means Christ gave up the possession of divine attributes not merely their use
heresies.summary: The heretical form of Kenotic theology teaches that Christ literally surrendered or gave up his divine attributes — omniscience, omnipotence, omnipresence — at the Incarnation, making him less than fully God during his earthly life. This contradicts Chalcedonian Christology, which affirms Christ as fully divine and fully human simultaneously. If Christ was not fully God incarnate, the atonement and resurrection lose their divine weight.

heresies.name: Kenosis (Moderate/Orthodox Form)
heresies.council_condemnation: None — this position is considered compatible with Chalcedonian Christology by mainstream Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant theologians
fingerprints: Christ voluntarily chose not to exercise or access his divine attributes during his earthly ministry
Christ retained full divine nature during the Incarnation but willingly limited the use of divine prerogatives
The self-emptying of Philippians 2:7 refers to Christ setting aside the independent exercise of divine attributes not their possession
Christ's expressions of human limitation — hunger, tiredness, not knowing the day or hour — reflect voluntary self-restriction not ontological diminishment
The kenosis was an act of divine condescension and humility not a surrender of divine nature
Christ remained fully God while genuinely experiencing human limitation by choice
heresies.summary: The moderate or orthodox form of Kenotic theology holds that Christ voluntarily chose not to independently exercise his divine attributes during his earthly ministry — setting aside their use rather than surrendering their possession. This is considered compatible with Chalcedonian Christology by Catholic, Orthodox, and mainstream Protestant traditions. It explains Christ's genuine human experiences of limitation without compromising his full divinity. This entry is included to help the app distinguish orthodox kenotic statements from the heretical form above.
